title: Localization by the finite inverse-gadget pushout
statement:
Use simplicial sets, standard simplices, coherent functor categories and equivalence edges of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and localization at edges of [def-coef-universally-localizing-simplicial-map]. Let $Q$ be the degreewise pushout
$$Q=\Delta^3\amalg_{\Delta^{\{0,2\}}\amalg\Delta^{\{1,3\}}}(\Delta^0\amalg\Delta^0),$$
where each of the two indicated edges is collapsed to its own point, and let $e:\Delta^1\to Q$ be the image of the edge $\{1,2\}$ of $\Delta^3$. For every small simplicial set $C$ and every collection $W\subseteq C_1$, regard each $w\in W$ as its representing simplicial map $\Delta^1\to C$ and form the degreewise pushout
$$D=C\amalg_{\coprod_{w\in W}\Delta^1}\coprod_{w\in W}Q.$$
Then the canonical map $j:C\to D$ exhibits $D$ as a localization of $C$ at $W$: for every quasicategory $E$, restriction $j^*:\operatorname{Fun}(D,E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(C,E)$ factors through the full subcategory on diagrams inverting $W$ and is a coherent functor equivalence onto that subcategory. Neither $C$ nor $D$ is assumed to be a quasicategory.

source.place: Corollary 6.3.2.9, with Q and e written out from Corollaries 6.3.2.7 (05ZJ) and 6.3.2.8 (05ZK); Kerodon tag, not a Stacks tag; read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED.

proof.text: Write $A$ and $B$ for the two vertices of $Q$, respectively the classes of $\{0,2\}$ and $\{1,3\}$. They are distinct. The map $e$ carries the endpoints of $\Delta^1$ to $B,A$. It is degreewise injective: the simplices of $\Delta^1$ are weakly increasing strings of its two vertices. A nonconstant string maps to a string in $\{1,2\}$ using both entries; it lies in neither collapsed edge, so the pushout identifies it with no other simplex. The two constant strings map to different vertices and their degeneracies. Hence $e$ and its coproduct over any small $W$ are monomorphisms.

source.place: 05ZL opening monomorphism check, expanded degree by degree using the quotient in 05ZJ.

proof.text: For any simplicial map $F:Q\to E$ into a quasicategory, write $a,b,c$ for the images of the edges $01,12,23$. Thus $a,c:F(A)\to F(B)$ and $b:F(B)\to F(A)$. The faces $012$ and $123$, whose long edges are collapsed, give $[b][a]=1_{F(A)}$ and $[c][b]=1_{F(B)}$ in the homotopy category supplied by [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Associativity gives $[a]=[c][b][a]=[c]$, and then $[a][b]=1_{F(B)}$. Thus $[b]$ is invertible. The same cited statement identifies invertibility of its component with the inverse-triangle definition of an equivalence edge. Consequently $F(e)=b$ is an equivalence. Restriction along $e$ therefore factors simplicially through the full subcategory $H(E)\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,E)$ on equivalence edges: this condition holds at each vertex of every parameter simplex.

source.place: 05ZK: the distinguished edge is inverted; explicit inverse equations from faces 012 and 123.

proof.text: The constant-arrow functor $k_1:E\to H(E)$ is a coherent equivalence. Indeed evaluation $v_0:H(E)\to E$ at the source satisfies $v_0k_1=1_E$. The monotone map $m:[1]\times[1]\to[1]$, $m(s,t)=\min(s,t)$, induces a coherent transformation $\eta:k_1v_0\to1_{H(E)}$: its component at an arrow $f:x\to y$ is the square with vertical edges $1_x$ and $f$. The formula for all parameters is evaluation of the universal arrow after $m$ on the arrow and homotopy coordinates, keeping all diagram coordinates unchanged; it therefore commutes with every simplicial operator. At both parameter endpoints the objects are in $H(E)$, so fullness makes it a transformation in $H(E)$. Functor and full-subcategory fibrancy follow from [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. By [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences] the square is an equivalence in the arrow category, since $1_x,f$ are equivalences. Its inverse and inverse triangles remain in the full subcategory $H(E)$. Applying the same pointwise statement to $\eta$ shows it is a coherent natural equivalence. This supplies the second quasi-inverse equation for $k_1$.

source.place: 05ZK reduction to Example 6.3.1.14; explicit proof that collapsing the interval localizes its sole nondegenerate edge.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-inverse-gadget-categorical-contractibility], the constant-diagram map $k_Q:E\to\operatorname{Fun}(Q,E)$ is a coherent equivalence. Let $r:\operatorname{Fun}(Q,E)\to H(E)$ be the factor of $e^*$ from step 2. Then $rk_Q=k_1$ exactly, since restricting a constant diagram is constant. Choose coherent quasi-inverses $u_Q$ of $k_Q$ and $u_1$ of $k_1$. The functor $s=k_Q u_1$ is a quasi-inverse to $r$: $rs=k_1u_1\simeq1$, while the counit $k_Qu_Q\simeq1$ gives $r\simeq k_1u_Q$ and hence $sr\simeq k_Qu_1k_1u_Q\simeq k_Qu_Q\simeq1$. Here $\operatorname{Fun}(Q,E)$, $H(E)$ and the functor simplicial sets between them are quasicategories by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Whiskering by a functor is a simplicial map of functor simplicial sets, so it carries an inverse edge and its two inverse-triangle $2$-simplices to the same data. Concatenation of two equivalence edges is a filler of an inner $2$-horn, and by [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] its class is the composite of two invertible classes in the homotopy category, hence again an equivalence edge. Therefore $e$ localizes $\Delta^1$ at its nondegenerate edge, with the entire functor-category property of [def-coef-universally-localizing-simplicial-map].

source.place: 05ZK proof, using 05ZJ; the quasi-inverse calculation is written explicitly.

proof.text: Put $A_W=\coprod_{w\in W}\Delta^1$, $B_W=\coprod_{w\in W}Q$ and $i=\coprod e$. Let $V$ consist of the one distinguished nondegenerate edge in each component of $A_W$. Degreewise, a map $(\coprod K_w)\times\Delta^n\to E$ is exactly a family of maps $K_w\times\Delta^n\to E$, compatibly with simplicial operators. Hence the restriction $i^*$ is the product of the restrictions $r$ from step 4, and its edge-inverting full subcategory is $\prod_{w\in W}H(E)$. Taking products of the explicit quasi-inverses and of their inverse equivalences proves that $i$ is a localization at $V$. The inverse triangles are coordinatewise inverse triangles, so no mere equivalence on cores or on homotopy categories is substituted. When $W$ is empty both products are the terminal simplicial set and the assertion is the identity.

source.place: 05ZL final sentence, Remark 6.3.1.15 (05ZC); direct coproduct-to-product calculation.

proof.text: Let $f:A_W\to C$ be the map representing the edges $w$. Apply [lem-coef-localization-monomorphic-pushout] to the following map of spans: $(X_{01},X_0,X_1)=(A_W,A_W,C)$, with legs $1,f$, and $(Y_{01},Y_0,Y_1)=(A_W,B_W,C)$, with legs $i,f$. Set $(p_{01},p_0,p_1)=(1,i,1)$ and $(V_{01},V_0,V_1)=(\varnothing,V,\varnothing)$. The spans commute strictly. The required monomorphisms are $1_{A_W}$ and $i$, established in step 1. The maps $p_{01},p_1$ localize at the empty collection because their restriction functors are identities; $p_0$ localizes at $V$ by step 5. Both conditions on the images of $V_{01}$ are vacuous. The source pushout is canonically $C$ and the target pushout is exactly $D$. The resulting edge collection is $f(V)=W$, including when an edge $w$ is degenerate. The induced map is exactly $j:C\to D$. The cited conclusion therefore gives the required factorization and coherent equivalence onto all $W$-inverting diagrams for every $E$, without assuming $C$ or $D$ quasicategorical.
